card.problem_text:
L-shape example (Lederer & Stenberg, weakly symmetric mixed elements, Sec. 7.1): adaptive mixed FEM against an exact corner-singular solution, ν = 0.3 and ν = 0.4999.
Geometry: 2D L-shaped domain (a rotated square with a smaller rotated square removed), Ω = {|x|+|y| ≤ 2^{1/2} l} \ {|x − 2^{−1/2} l| + |y| ≤ 2^{−1/2} l}, with l = 1. The re-entrant corner is at the origin.
Material: Linear isotropic elasticity (not hyperelastic) under plane strain. E = 1, with ν = 0.3 (moderate case) or ν = 0.4999 (nearly incompressible case). Lamé parameters come from the standard formulas λ = Eν/((1+ν)(1−2ν)) and µ = E/(2(1+ν)).
Boundary conditions: Not stated explicitly. The problem is taken from Section 10.3.2 of [36], and the boundary data presumably come from the exact solution given there. The displacement is fixed only up to rigid-body motions.
Loading: Manufactured/exact singular solution: u_x and u_y vary as r^α trigonometric forms, with α = 0.544483737 and Q = 0.543075579. Body force and boundary data are not given explicitly; they follow from the exact solution in [36].
Discretisation in the paper: Adaptive refinement of a triangular mesh (SOLVE→ESTIMATE→MARK→REFINE). An element is marked if its local estimator is ≥ 1/4 of the maximum. Four weakly symmetric mixed elements are used: SGG2 and SGG3 (Stenberg/Gopalakrishnan–Guzmán, k = 2, 3), AFW (Arnold–Falk–Winther, k = 2) and RAFW (method (3.22), k = 2). A uniform refinement is also run as a comparison. The initial mesh, element counts and DOF counts are not stated.
Features: Re-entrant corner of the L-shaped domain at the origin. The exact stress behaves like r^(α−1) with α = 0.5445 < 1, so it is unbounded at the corner, and the solution has only H^s regularity with s < 1.54..
Question: which of these quantities can serve as trustworthy reference values: e_σC (stress error) (Error of the discrete stress against the exact stress, in the paper's C-weighted norm. Reported as a convergence curve against N for ν = 0.3 and ν = 0.4999.); e_uC (displacement error) (Error of the discrete displacement in the paper's C-type norm.); e^mean_C (Mean-type error measure; its precise definition is not in this section.); η (a posteriori estimator, Theorem 7), adaptive and uniform (Global error estimator under adaptive and under uniform refinement.); e_σinc, e_uinc, η_inc (incompressible-robust errors and estimator, Theorem 8) (Errors in ν-robust norms and the relative estimator for the incompressible setting, at ν = 0.4999.)?

spec.name: Lederer–Stenberg Sec. 7.1: L-shaped domain, adaptive weakly symmetric mixed FEM vs. exact corner-singular solution (ν = 0.3 and ν = 0.4999)
spec.geometry: 2D L-shaped domain Ω = {|x|+|y| ≤ √2·l} \ {|x − l/√2| + |y| ≤ l/√2}, l = 1 (a rotated square with a smaller rotated square removed). There is one re-entrant corner at the origin, and its interior angle is presumably 3π/2. The paper discretises it with triangular meshes refined adaptively (SOLVE→ESTIMATE→MARK→REFINE, with maximum marking at θ = 1/4) and also with uniform refinement for comparison.
spec.material: Linear isotropic elasticity under plane strain. This is not hyperelastic and is outside the pipeline's usual nonlinear scope. E = 1 and ν ∈ {0.3, 0.4999}. λ = Eν/((1+ν)(1−2ν)) and µ = E/(2(1+ν)). At ν = 0.4999, λ/µ ≈ 5·10^3 (nearly incompressible), so the problem needs locking-free, ν-robust norms and estimators.
spec.loading: Manufactured exact singular solution from Sec. 10.3.2 of ref. [36]. Displacement components are r^α times trigonometric functions of θ, with α = 0.544483737 and Q = 0.543075579. Body force and boundary data (Dirichlet and/or traction) are implied by the exact solution but not given in this section. The statement 'displacement fixed only up to rigid-body motions' suggests a pure-traction (Neumann) problem, which would need load compatibility and handling of rigid-body modes.
qois: e_σC: global C-weighted norm of the stress error against the exact stress. TRUSTWORTHY as a reference quantity. It is an integral norm, finite because σ ∈ L2 (|σ|² ~ r^{2α−2} is integrable in 2D). The exact solution allows it to be evaluated without a reference mesh. Expected rate: under uniform refinement about N^{−α/2} ≈ N^{−0.27}, limited by the singularity, not the element order. Under adaptive refinement, recovery of the optimal N^{−k/2} rate. Caveat: quadrature near r = 0 must resolve the integrable singularity. Pointwise or peak stress at the corner is NOT a valid QoI (unbounded, ~r^{α−1}).

e_uC: displacement error in the C-type norm. TRUSTWORTHY: u ∈ H^{1+α−ε}, and the error is a global norm computed from the exact solution. It converges at least as fast as the stress error. It needs the rigid-body modes fixed consistently between the discrete and exact solutions; if they are not, the error is not well defined.

e^mean_C: mean-type error measure. NOT ASSESSABLE as stated: its definition is not given in this section. If it is a mean-value or region-average error it would converge, but this cannot be confirmed.

η (Theorem 7 estimator), adaptive and uniform: NOT a reference value. It is a computed upper bound. It is meaningful for checking reliability and efficiency through the efficiency index η/e against the exact error, and for comparing adaptive and uniform rates. Its trustworthiness depends on the Theorem 7 constants, which may depend on λ, so it may not be robust at ν = 0.4999.

e_σinc, e_uinc, η_inc (Theorem 8, ν-robust norms/estimator) at ν = 0.4999: TRUSTWORTHY as global error norms against the exact solution, with the same singular-rate behaviour as above. η_inc is to be judged through its efficiency index, which Theorem 8 claims is uniform in λ.
well_posedness: The boundary conditions are not stated. With pure traction, the problem is well posed only if the loads are compatible (zero net force and moment) and the rigid-body modes are fixed, e.g. by a constraint or by orthogonality to them. With Dirichlet data taken from the exact solution, it is well posed without extra constraints.

Material stability: linear isotropic with µ > 0 and λ > 0. Stable for both ν values. At ν = 0.4999 the λ-dependence of the constants matters, so only ν-robust norms and estimators (Theorem 8) give λ-uniform statements.
No limit points or load-level issues: the problem is linear, so the solution depends linearly on the data.

Singular feature: the re-entrant corner at the origin, with σ ~ r^{α−1}, α ≈ 0.5445 < 1. σ is unbounded but in L2, and u ∈ H^{1+s} with s < α. Global energy-type norms (e_σC, e_uC, e_inc) converge. Pointwise or peak corner stress does not converge and must not be used as a QoI.
Under uniform refinement, rates are capped by the singularity (about N^{−α/2}) regardless of k. Optimal rates can only be recovered with adaptive, corner-graded meshes.
Exact-error evaluation requires quadrature that resolves the r^{α−1} integrand near the corner. Otherwise the 'exact' reference errors themselves are polluted.

steps.detail: The geometry can be drawn as a polygon: the L-shape has vertices (-√2,0), (0,-√2), (√2/2,-√2/2), (0,0), (√2/2,√2/2), (0,√2), with l = 1. The loading cannot be represented. This is a manufactured-solution test. The boundary data come from an exact corner-singular field whose displacement varies as r^α with trigonometric terms, α = 0.544483737. Applied on any boundary edge, that data is non-constant, and the needed body force is not given. The pipeline accepts only constant tractions, pressures and constant prescribed displacements on straight segments, with no body force. The problem says outright that boundary conditions, body force and boundary data are not stated and must come from [36]. Using constant data would solve a different problem and quietly change it. Also, every quantity asked about measures error against the exact solution in the paper's norms, or is an a posteriori estimator. None of them is a physical response, such as a displacement at a point, that this pipeline could reproduce and compare against a reference. The estimators η and η_inc and the measure e^mean_C also depend on the method (SGG2/3, AFW, RAFW mixed elements), and e^mean_C is not even defined in the section. The nearly incompressible case (ν = 0.4999) is also above the pipeline's limit of ν ≤ 0.49. So none of the listed quantities can serve as a reference value in this pipeline.

assumptions: I chose the ν = 0.3 case because ν = 0.4999 is above the pipeline's limit of 0.49.

The outer vertices are the set difference of the two rotated squares with l = 1, rounded to 8 decimals. The removed square shares its two edges at (√2,0) with the outer square, which leaves a 270° re-entrant corner at the origin.
